feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital platform leadership and credible progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows solid scope, but impact would be stronger with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter structure, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: the progression from coordinator to director is credible and supports the “senior digital leader” brand.  
- Strong domain relevance: public-sector communications, Drupal modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI search are consistently aligned.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools add credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, reduced publishing time, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Simplify and de-duplicate structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve scannability. The “Recent Projects” footer is valuable but would work better as a dedicated section.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” and “member-facing” are hyphenated correctly, but style is slightly inconsistent across bullets. “Ranked among the top public universities…” under Education feels generic and can be removed. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning that aligns well with the experience section, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and skills sections. Tightening it and adding one concrete scope marker would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Consider a sharper version: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Builds governance models, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve how mission-driven institutions publish, measure, and scale digital communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more direct verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling.”
- Use parallel structure in the second sentence; the current list is strong but long.
- If space allows, add one concrete scale cue from recent work (for example, “10,000+ page website” or “3.5M annual page views”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Digital leader” is close to the subtitle; avoid repeating the same positioning language verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and use parallel phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Consider replacing “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- Change “operations” in multiple lines if possible to avoid repetition; “leadership,” “production,” or “optimization” adds variety.
- Keep this section high-level; let the Technical + IT and Topline Skills sections carry tools and platform specifics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming to 6 core areas.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and foregrounding outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish freelance work from earlier roles.
- Standardize parallel structure: start each item with a strong action verb and keep each to one concise outcome-focused sentence.
- Replace vague phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” with clearer value, e.g., “built for reuse and future campaign expansion.”
- Consider this tighter version: AI Hybrid Search — Led development of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery. We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and reusable modules. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Produced an ongoing advocacy video series across planning, production, and distribution for web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and Advocacy Video Series overlap with Work Experience bullets; keep footer phrasing shorter and more project-specific.
- “Built/developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs slightly for better rhythm.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets into outcome-led statements, e.g. “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Make technical work more concise and senior: “Improved enterprise web operations through CMS development, front-end implementation, analytics, and troubleshooting for high-traffic public-facing properties.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, users reached, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search success gains, or engagement improvements from the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI-enabled search, microsites, and anniversary/campaign work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo the summary and NACo role—avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, video operations, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes and scope: “Led redesign and Drupal migration of a 10,000+ page website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific or measurable: include email list size, engagement lift, social growth, or campaign results if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built reporting stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep focus here on strategic leadership, systems, and transformation.
- Video production appears in multiple NACo roles; frame this item around building the in-house studio, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the associate-director level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets and front-load outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role’s opening line.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the 2015–2018 role and the Recent Projects section.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and consistency: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems/automation over basic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in the item itself: **enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If one platform was primary in the 2022–2024 director role, place it first to reflect recency and strongest hands-on relevance

- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands of recipients,” or channel leadership here; those are already covered in Work Experience

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to platforms/methods and make the wording more precise.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the detailed list here and shortening the Topline version to broader capabilities.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify scope: mention 2–3 channels only, e.g., “supported web, email, social, and livestream/video production workflows.”
- Add measurable outputs where possible: number of livestreams, cadence of weekly videos, size/timing of website refresh, or team support (“mentored 1 associate”).
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and video. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on launching/building the function, not scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; use “formalize” or “help establish” here instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:

- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and use stronger verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools

- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
